## Summary

Test-first contract for the follow-source interface and unlock/persistence logic using a mocked Steamworks session, written before the implementation features (F3/F4). Defines the interface the renderer and unlock logic consume so the Steam SDK stays behind an abstraction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A mockable `FollowSource` interface is defined (init, isSteamAvailable, openStorePage, isFollowing, claim) with a deterministic fake implementation.
- [ ] Unit tests (`tests/steam-follow/`) cover: follow detected → unlock flow triggered; already-unlocked → no re-verification prompt; Steam absent → graceful degraded path (no crash); choose-one-of-three catalog resolution; unlock persistence round-trip across simulated launches.
- [ ] Tests run and pass under `--project unit` (fast, no browser).
- [ ] The interface contract documents that the renderer never imports the Steam SDK directly.

## Minimal Implementation

- Test-only feature: interface + test doubles + unit tests.
- Reference the launcher item's content-locator abstraction (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) for the dependency-injection pattern.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (launcher) for the abstraction pattern it establishes.

## Deliverables

- `FollowSource` interface + mocked unit tests.

# Feature: Per-game repos use `src/` source root with alias-based core imports (Option C)

Part of epic CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17. Follow-on refinement of the F4 game-repo scaffold.

## Goal

As a game developer I can clone a `tce-<game>` repo and find that game's source at the repo-root `src/` directory, with every engine import going through the `@core-engine/*` (and `@card-system/*`, `@rule-engine/*`, `@ui/*`, `@ai/*`) path aliases, so that the repo has an idiomatic layout and does not rely on the `src -> ../tableau-card-engine-core/src` compatibility symlink or fragile `../../src/**` relative imports.

## Problem

The F4 scaffold keeps the game nested at `example-games/<game>/` and creates a `src` symlink into the core checkout. 319 game-source imports use `../../src/**` and only resolve because the game sits exactly two levels below the repo root. This is fragile, non-idiomatic, and blocks moving the game source to `src/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Decision record exists (child C1) fixing the per-game layout (`src/**` or `src/<game>/**`), how `scripts/`, `example-games/gym`, shared assets and test helpers resolve from `src/`, and the `scenePath` contract for monorepo-local vs sibling-repo contexts.
2. A scaffolded `tce-<game>` checkout has its game source under `src/`, contains no `src` symlink to the core, and `npm run build` + `npm test -- --project unit` succeed.
3. No game-repo source or test imports core through a `../../src/**` relative specifier; a test/lint guards this invariant.
4. The launcher (`configs/*.json` presets + `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`) resolves game scenes in both the flat monorepo (`example-games/<game>/…`) and the `src/` sibling game-repo layout; the 1-game (`solo`) and all-games (`full`) presets both build.
5. `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `README.md` describe the new per-game layout.

## Constraints

- The monorepo/launcher flat layout may stay `example-games/<game>/`; only per-game repos change to `src/`. C1 may override this if a uniform layout proves cleaner.
- The producer gate on F4 still applies: no GitHub repo creation or push.
- Engine imports must resolve via `tsconfig.json` `paths` + Vite `resolve.alias`; no new npm publication of the engine.

## Children

- C1 Decide per-game `src/` layout, import contract and preset resolution
- C2 Codemod game source + tests off `../../src/**` to engine aliases
- C3 Extraction/scaffold/repo-layout emit the `src/` layout
- C4 Discovery plugin + launcher presets resolve `src/` sibling layouts
- C5 Update game docs and verify per-game tsc/build/unit
data.title: F9: Per-game repos use src/ source root with alias-based core imports (Option C)

# Task C3: Extraction/scaffold/repo-layout emit the `src/` layout

Parent: F9 CG-0MUH0NTRG007GDME (part of epic CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17).
Depends on: C1 (layout + import contract).

## Goal

As a distribution/engine maintainer I can run the extraction + scaffold so a `tce-<game>` checkout places the game source at `src/` per the C1 decision and does not create a `src` symlink into the core.

## Scope

1. `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` — update each game's `paths` (and any asset/path fields) to the agreed `src/` layout so extraction produces the new tree.
2. `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — stop emitting the `src -> core/src` symlink; place/repoint the game tree at `src/`; adjust `configs/game.json`, `tsconfig.json` include/exclude, and `vite.config.ts` if needed; keep the remaining symlinks required by C1 (`scripts`, `example-games/gym`, `tests/helpers`, `core`, shared assets) or replace them per the contract.
3. Update the scaffold unit tests (`tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`) to assert the new layout and the absence of the `src` symlink.
4. Verify `scripts/extract-repos.sh --dry-run --target <game>` and a real scaffold for golf and main-street produce the `src/` layout.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `repo-layout.json` and `game-repo-scaffold.ts` implement the C1 layout; scaffold unit tests updated and green.
2. A scaffolded golf (and main-street) checkout has game source under `src/` and no `src` symlink; `tsc --noEmit` + `npm run build` succeed.
3. Extraction history preservation is unchanged (still via `git filter-repo`; counts recorded).
4. `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5 updated to describe the emitted layout.

## Key Files

- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json`
- `scripts/extract-repos.sh`
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`, `tests/scripts/extract-repos.test.ts`
data.title: C3: Extraction/scaffold/repo-layout emit the src/ layout
